sections.name: DocumentProcessingStatus, DocumentKind, VerificationStatus, TimelineStatus, CaseLocation
sections.title: Status labels and case location
sections.what: Lists the allowed status words for documents, checks and timelines, the document kinds, and the location of a case by district, circle and village. It also describes a basic case, a land parcel, a family member and a relationship between members.
sections.why: Fixed word lists stop typos from creating new statuses that the screens would not understand.
sections.watch_out: Each status word must match exactly across the app, so renaming one here means changing every place that uses it.

sections.name: VerificationItem, SurveyRecord, GuidanceAction, NextAction, GuidanceStatus, GuidanceChecklistItem
sections.title: Checks, guidance and review shapes
sections.what: Describes a verification item and its outcome, a survey record, guidance actions and checklists, a review packet with its comparison values, timeline events, the government process context, the full case detail, and records imported from official sources. Each is marked as synthetic or demonstration where relevant.
sections.why: These shapes let the app show checks and next steps in a consistent way, and mark demo data so it is not mistaken for official records.
sections.watch_out: The review packet and official parcel record lines are cut off in the packet, so their full fields are unknown here.

summary: Defines the data shapes for a land case: people, parcels, documents, checks, guidance, review packets and the timeline.
purpose: Gives one shared description of everything a case holds, so the screens and server code agree on the same fields.
why: Shared types stop the parts of the app from drifting apart. Likely reason: the app relies on typed data across many files. Reason not stated in the code.
how: The file exports type labels for statuses, locations, documents, extracted facts, verification items, guidance, review packets, official records and the full case detail. Other code uses these labels when it reads or writes case data.
inputs: None directly. Other code fills these shapes.
outputs: None directly. The labels guide the checker and the editor.
risks: The packet cuts off the ReviewPacket and OfficialParcelRecord definitions, so some fields are not visible here. Adding required fields can break existing data.
debug: If a value is rejected as the wrong type, find its type name here and compare the fields. Check the cut-off lines in the full file.
